hook: A U.S. Air Force ISR aircraft from the 482nd Attack Squadron logged a UAP observation via Full Motion Video at 1732Z on September 16, 2020, during a 20-hour-56-minute surveillance mission over the Arabian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz, and Gulf of Oman in support of NAVCENT.
why_it_matters: This MISREP is significant because it documents a UAP observation embedded within an otherwise routine military ISR mission, with the observation formally recorded through standardized military reporting channels and later submitted to AARO. The mission also recorded two separate electromagnetic interference events of unknown origin causing complete lost-link and flight path deviations, which occurred in the same operational area as the UAP. The combination of an anomalous observation, unexplained EMI events, and repeated Iranian Air Defense intercepts in a single mission log provides unusually dense context around the UAP sighting.

key_findings.finding: A UAP was observed via Full Motion Video (FMV) at 1732Z on September 16, 2020, in the vicinity of grid reference 39RVM5 in the Strait of Hormuz region. The observing aircraft was at FL180 traveling at 90 KIAS at the time.

key_findings.finding: Iranian Air Defense hailed the aircraft on guard frequency three times during the mission — twice with a directive tone (0408Z and 0421Z at FL180) and once with a professional tone (1141Z at FL040). The aircraft responded with standard responses each time, with no mission impact reported.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: This MISREP was formally submitted through standardized UAP reporting channels to AARO, as explicitly described in the document's official manifest, making it a direct example of the military-to-AARO reporting pipeline.
The document was declassified and released as part of USCENTCOM MOR 26-0019 in January 2026 under the PURSUE UAP disclosure initiative, which is driven by congressional UAP transparency legislation.
